options.help: the state dump: the live setting overrides (the toggles, the caps, the log surface — the tokens apart) as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on the request dump command and the graceful shutdown; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command

options.name: dump-key
options.setting-help: the key that seals the state dumps (the reload's state file too) (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
options.help: the key that seals the state dumps and the reload's state file: the state rides encrypted (an HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream, authenticated — a restore refuses a wrong or missing key, and a configured key refuses an unsealed dump); the reload re-exec re-resolves the same key, so the state file reads on the other side; no key = the dumps stay 0600 plaintext with the integrity hash; a dump path without a key warns at start and on set; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)
